disposition_mapping.rationale: Extraction carries no judgment once the period is locked; council consensus (pragmatist, finance_domain, agentic_architect, emerging_economy with conditions) merges it with comparatives-loading into one automated ingestion step. The merge is conditioned on retaining locked-period actuals as an explicit input, structural inability to read an unlocked period (KB-03), and a named analyst who owns exceptions and a routine (not merely failure-triggered) reconciliation check, reflecting emerging_economy's heterogeneous-ledger concern.

Same deterministic-pull reasoning as VAR-01; the approved budget version and latest forecast remain explicit, separately traceable inputs to the merged ingestion step, satisfying VAR-R-02, with version-ambiguity halting rather than silent fallback.

The council held firmly (accounting_standards, finance_domain, pragmatist, hitl_designer, agentic_architect) that computation must remain a distinct, auditable step from threshold screening, because KB-06/KB-07/KB-08 require the policy basis and FX isolation to be visible and separately reported, not folded into an undifferentiated engine. The arithmetic is automated, but policy/FX versioning and disclosure-on-change are now explicit outputs, strengthening rather than diluting the control.

Against maximalist's and emerging_economy's proposed merger with computation, the majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards) held that materiality selection must remain a separately inspectable decision point with its own output, or VAR-R-04's actor-separation becomes nominal rather than real. The automated percentage/absolute test is preserved, but a mandatory analyst override surface and exclusion log are added so the selection remains a live judgment function, not a silent filter.

Near-unanimous council rejection of maximalist's AI-drafted candidate explanations: commentary authorship must stay with the accountable budget holder because the explanation is an attestation about business reality a model cannot make on another's behalf. Automation is confined to orchestration (reminders, escalation, channel-agnostic submission per emerging_economy), not content generation.

Council majority (pragmatist, hitl_designer, finance_domain) held that narrative assembly must remain an accountable human output even though templated auto-population of tables and verbatim commentary is a legitimate, low-risk efficiency gain; traceability of an LLM draft to source records (agentic_architect's argument) tells you the draft didn't fabricate facts, not that it characterized the variance correctly, so authorship accountability is preserved with the FP&A analyst.

Review and challenge survives per VAR-R-07, but its scope is materially widened per hitl_designer, finance_domain and agentic_architect: it must now receive the materiality override log, policy/FX version log and commentary provenance, not just the polished draft, or the reviewer is only checking prose rather than substance. Actor remains the FP&A manager, structurally distinct from TS-03's analyst, satisfying VAR-R-04.

Council majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, emerging_economy) rejected maximalist's auto-publish-on-signoff design: distribution mechanics can be automated and made bandwidth-appropriate, but authorization is a distinct, loggable event and the manager remains the named accountable actor for release and for defending the figures, with a retained record of what was sent, to whom, and when.

steps.description: An automated, connector-driven pipeline, triggered by the period-lock event, pulls actuals from the closed-period ledger and the approved budget version and latest forecast from the planning system in a single pass. The pipeline is structurally restricted to locked-period data and cannot read from an open or preliminary period. Every pull is logged with source system, timestamp and a content hash for replayability. Because actuals and comparatives in many group structures arrive via heterogeneous local ledgers, manual journal backlogs or spreadsheet-based plans, the step produces a routine version/lock reconciliation output every cycle (not only on hard failure), which a named FP&A analyst reviews. The analyst owns an exception queue for failed loads, unresolved budget/forecast version ambiguity, or any attempted pull against an unlocked period; the pipeline halts and escalates to this analyst rather than guessing a version.
steps.name: Ingest and reconcile actuals and comparatives

steps.description: A deterministic calculation engine, configured and reviewed by the FP&A analyst, computes price, volume and mix variances against the actuals and comparatives datasets, using the accounting policies applied to actuals and the constant-currency exchange-rate table as explicit, versioned inputs. The FX effect is isolated and reported as its own distinct line, never netted into price, volume or mix. Every output figure carries a record of the policy version and FX-rate-table version that produced it. Any divergence from the prior period's policy or FX version is flagged as an explicit disclosure trigger, not a silent log entry, so policy drift cannot be quietly re-baselined.
steps.name: Compute price, volume, mix and FX variances
outputs: Policy or FX change disclosure flag

steps.description: An automated threshold engine screens the variance dataset against the percentage and absolute materiality criteria to produce the candidate population for explanation. This remains a separately inspectable step, distinct from computation and from review, so that a reviewer or auditor can ask whether a variance was screened out because it was genuinely immaterial or because an upstream mis-tag pushed it below threshold. The accountable FP&A analyst retains explicit override authority: they may pull in sub-threshold items judged qualitatively significant, and must log documented reasoning whenever they exclude an agent-flagged item. Threshold values themselves are human-owned configuration, versioned and logged on change. This step's actor is structurally distinct from the actor who later reviews and challenges the report.
steps.name: Apply materiality thresholds with override authority

steps.description: Budget holders remain the sole authors of variance explanations; no generative drafting of candidate narratives is introduced, because an explanation of business reality is an attestation that cannot be made on someone else's behalf. An orchestration agent dispatches variance-specific requests, tracks deadlines, sends escalating reminders, and timestamps receipt, escalating non-response to the FP&A manager with the item marked outstanding rather than auto-filled. Structured email/template submission remains a first-class channel alongside any portal, so budget holders with intermittent connectivity or no platform seat are not forced through a single collaborative tool.
steps.name: Obtain budget holder commentary

steps.description: Variance tables and attested commentary are auto-populated into a report template, eliminating manual rebuilding of decks, but the FP&A analyst remains the accountable assembler of the narrative draft. The analyst can be tool-assisted (e.g., auto-drafted variance tables, verbatim commentary insertion) but is responsible for noticing missing or inconsistent explanations, mislabeled drivers, and for standing behind the draft as its named author. The draft retains visible linkage to the policy-consistent, FX-isolated figures and the materiality override log that produced it.
steps.name: Consolidate and draft variance report

steps.description: An FP&A manager, distinct from whoever applied materiality thresholds, reviews and challenges the draft report. The manager's inputs are deliberately widened beyond the polished narrative: they receive the materiality override/exclusion log (what was pulled in or screened out and why), the policy/FX version log, and the commentary provenance record, so the review can interrogate the selection and computation decisions, not just the prose. This is the control gate against everything upstream, including any tool-assisted drafting, and is not automated or merged with drafting or selection.
steps.name: Review and challenge

steps.description: Distribution mechanics (formatting, publishing, archiving with full provenance chain) are automated and use bandwidth-appropriate formats so recipients on constrained connections are not excluded, but publication cannot occur without the manager's explicit, logged sign-off event from TS-06 — there is no auto-publish on review completion alone. The manager remains the named, accountable actor for authorizing release and for standing behind the figures in any live presentation or Q&A; presentation mechanics may be on-demand, but authorization and accountability for the distributed artifact are mandatory, recurring human functions, and the record of what was sent, to whom, and when is retained as a distinct, auditable event.
steps.name: Authorize, present and distribute to management
